s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly growing vascular tumor on the scalp
salient_findings: 8-mm red, firm, mobile nodule on the left temporal scalp
Irregular red lacunae with irregular vessels and absence of septa on dermoscopic evaluation
Well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor with ectatic thin-walled vessels and intravascular branching papillary structures on histopathology
key_facts: The patient is a man in his 40s
The patient has no significant medical history
The tumor is located on the left temporal scalp
The tumor is 8-mm in size
The tumor is red, firm, and mobile
Dermoscopic evaluation shows irregular red lacunae and irregular vessels
Histopathology shows a well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor
The tumor extends to the superficial subcutaneous tissue
The tumor is composed of ectatic thin-walled vessels with intravascular branching papillary structures
The endothelial cells have numerous intracytoplasmic eosinophilic hyaline globules
PAS staining is positive for hyaline globules in the cytoplasm of endothelial cells
Tumor vessels are positive for CD-31 and negative for D2-40 and HHV-8

shortlist.label: Glomeruloid hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches dermoscopic and histopathological findings of irregular red lacunae, ectatic vessels, and intracytoplasmic hyaline globules

shortlist.label: Papillary intralymphatic angioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with vascular tumor morphology and presence of intravascular branching papillary structures

shortlist.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Shares features of well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor with ectatic thin-walled vessels and papillary structures

shortlist.label: Epithelioid hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible match given the presence of ectatic vessels and endothelial cell abnormalities

shortlist.label: Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: General category of vascular tumors, with specific subtypes potentially matching the case details

raw.rationale: The presence of intravascular branching papillary structures and numerous intracytoplasmic eosinophilic hyaline globules in the endothelial cells, as seen in the histopathology, are characteristic features of glomeruloid hemangioma.

rejected.label: Papillary intralymphatic angioendothelioma
rejected.why: The tumor vessels are positive for CD-31 and negative for D2-40, which does not support a lymphatic origin

rejected.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: The histopathology does not show the characteristic retiform pattern of this tumor

rejected.label: Epithelioid hemangioma
rejected.why: The endothelial cells do not exhibit the epithelioid morphology typical of this tumor

rejected.label: Hemangioma
rejected.why: The tumor's unique features, such as intravascular papillary structures and hyaline globules, are not typical of a common hemangioma
